# TI LP-MSPM0L1306 LaunchPad: what runs in 4 kB of RAM

> Disclosure: Fox Red Labs is a lab run by a TI employee on personal time. Contributors' projects are their own. Not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Texas Instruments or any other manufacturer.

**Short answer.** From a Mac terminal TI's blink example for the LP-MSPM0L1306 built in 3.3 seconds and flashed in 0.6, and the chip ran CoreMark at 78.27 per second at 32 MHz: per MHz, the same core speed as the MSPM0G3507. RAM is the limit on everything else: CoreMark fits with 144 bytes to spare, Zephyr's hello_world uses 94% of RAM (a trimmed Zephyr shell still fits, with 48 bytes left), 5 of 19 Embench benchmarks and the largest of four small neural nets do not fit.

Terms: [docs/vocab.md](../docs/vocab.md). Every problem found, with its cause and fix: [FAQ](FAQ.md). 1 kB = 1,024 bytes. **SysConfig** is TI's tool that writes a chip's setup code; **DriverLib** is TI's low-level C library for its peripherals; a **flash wait state** is an extra clock cycle the core waits for each read from flash at high clock speeds; **NONMAIN** is the chip's boot configuration area, which a bad write can lock for good; the **heap** is RAM handed out at run time by `malloc`; **MessagePack** is a compact binary form of JSON.

**First blink:** `./start.sh mspm0l1306 blink` from the top of a clone, once the four tools are installed ([One-command build](#one-command-build), [the tools](#where-these-facts-come-from)). Then: [what each part of the board is for](img/board-tour.png), the CoreMark and timing sources in `bench/coremark/` and `bench/timing/`, and [notes to copy into your own project for your AI assistant](AGENTS.md).

## What is in this folder

<!-- folder-contents -->
**In this folder:** this README; `AGENTS.md` (notes for an AI assistant, every line from a run); `FAQ.md` (every error hit, with its exact text and the fix). Folders: `bench/coremark/` and `bench/timing/` the CoreMark and timing sources, `color-player/` the color player, `freertos/` FreeRTOS builds, `img/` pictures, `third-party/` third-party benchmark code, `tools/` helper scripts for this board, `zephyr/` Zephyr builds. Results are rows in `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv` at the top of the repository, not in this folder.

**Not in this folder:** TI's SDK, CCStudio, SysConfig and the compilers (you install them; the versions are under "Where these facts come from"); built images (`.out`, `.hex`, `.bin`, `.elf`), which are not cleared for redistribution, so you build them with the command below.

**Taking this folder alone:** the one-command build runs from the top of a clone and the by-hand steps from inside this folder; both call `tools/` and `data/`, and the benchmarks also borrow sources from folders that several boards share. A sparse clone fetches only those, about 10 to 60 MB, instead of the whole repository (about 500 MB):

```bash
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/Fox-Red-Labs/fox-red-labs.git
cd fox-red-labs
git sparse-checkout add mspm0l1306 tools data mspm0g3507/mcu-bench third-party/coremark
```

`docs/` is left out on purpose (236 MB, mostly pictures). Read a page a link points to there with `git show HEAD:docs/<file>`, for example `git show HEAD:docs/vocab.md`.


## The board

| Part | Fact | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| Chip | MSPM0L1306: Arm Cortex-M0+ at up to 32 MHz from an internal oscillator (no PLL, no crystal needed) | Data sheet |
| Memory | 64 kB flash, 4 kB RAM, reported by the chip itself; device ID `0x1BB8202F` | Read from the chip |
| On the chip | One 12-bit ADC, two op-amps, a general-purpose amplifier, a comparator with an 8-bit DAC, hardware CRC, 3 DMA channels, four 16-bit timers, two UARTs, two I2C, one SPI | Data sheet |
| Not on the chip | No FPU, no divide instruction, no math accelerator, no AES, no random number generator | Data sheet |
| LEDs and buttons | An RGB LED, a red LED, two buttons | `AGENTS.md` |
| Sensors | A light sensor (photodiode into op-amp 0) and a thermistor | `AGENTS.md` |
| Debugger | Onboard XDS110, probe serial <probe serial>, firmware 3.0.0.43; two serial ports, no driver to install | this page, Where these facts come from |

![The LP-MSPM0L1306 with each part numbered: USB and debugger, J101, buttons S1 to S3, header pins, light sensor, thermistor, J16 and J17, the chip and the LEDs](img/board-tour.png)

MSPM0L1306: Arm Cortex-M0+ at up to 32 MHz from an internal oscillator (no PLL, no crystal needed), 64 kB flash, 4 kB RAM, one 12-bit ADC, two op-amps, a general-purpose amplifier, a comparator with an 8-bit DAC, hardware CRC, 3 DMA channels, four 16-bit timers, two UARTs, two I2C, one SPI. No FPU, no divide instruction, no math accelerator, no AES, no random number generator. The LaunchPad adds an RGB LED, a red LED, two buttons, a light sensor (photodiode into op-amp 0) and a thermistor. Read from the chip: device ID `0x1BB8202F`, 64 kB flash and 4 kB RAM reported by the chip itself.

It came with TI's out-of-box demo in flash. It is silent until asked: send it a MessagePack command and it streams the light sensor (339 to 343 counts on this bench) or the thermistor (22.8 °C). How: [FAQ](FAQ.md#the-out-of-box-demo-is-silent-on-the-serial-port-is-it-broken). The original image was saved first and put back at the end: all 64 kB of flash read back identical, and the demo answered over serial.

## Ten-minute path

Quickest: `./start.sh mspm0l1306 blink` from the top of the clone does all of this in one command ([One-command build](#one-command-build)). The steps below do it by hand (measured: build 3.3 s, flash 0.6 s).

1. **Plug in the board (bench).** It shows up as an XDS110 probe with two serial ports; no driver to install. Find its serial from the top of the clone with `python3 tools/frl/frl.py detect`.
2. **Copy TI's example (terminal).** These steps run from inside this folder. With the tools in Where these facts come from installed (`/Applications/ti/` is where TI's installer puts SDK 2.11.00.07 by default; some installs use `~/ti/`, so change the path if yours differs):

   ```bash
   cd mspm0l1306
   cp -R /Applications/ti/mspm0_sdk_2_11_00_07/examples/nortos/LP_MSPM0L1306/driverlib/gpio_toggle_output .
   ```
3. **Build it (terminal, 3.3 s).**

   ```bash
   ../mspm0g3507/mcu-bench/sdk-common/sdkmake.sh gpio_toggle_output/ticlang
   ```
4. **Flash it with OpenOCD (terminal, 0.6 s).** `tools/ocd.sh` uses only the probe you name and refuses to run without one. Put your serial from step 1 in place of `<serial>`:

   ```bash
   PROBE=<serial> tools/ocd.sh "reset halt" "program gpio_toggle_output/ticlang/gpio_toggle_output.out verify" "reset run"
   ```
5. **Look at the board (bench).** The RGB LED cycles. OpenOCD prints `Error: checksum mismatch - attempting binary compare` before `** Verified OK **`; that is normal ([FAQ](FAQ.md#openocd-prints-error-checksum-mismatch---attempting-binary-compare-did-the-flash-fail)). TI's UniFlash command line also works, in 15.0 s, with a connection file for your probe serial.

## One-command build

From the top of the clone:

```bash
./start.sh mspm0l1306 blink
```

It backs up the board, builds TI's blink, flashes it and checks the LED pattern through the debugger, with no assistant (`docs/frl.md`). It took 1 min 15 s from the command to a confirmed blink once the tools were installed (`data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `time_to_blink`, variant `oneline-terminal-start-sh`). If tools are missing it lists them with their sizes and stops. With several probes plugged in it stops with FRL-E002 and lists their serials; add `--probe <serial>`. It does not run the benchmarks does.

## What was measured

One LP-MSPM0L1306, run from a Mac terminal on 2026-10-06. Rows cite a test name in `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv` or a file.

| What | Number | Conditions | Level | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chip | 32 MHz, 64 kB flash, 4 kB RAM, 1.68 Msps ADC | Data sheet values | claim | Data sheet |
| Flash and RAM size, device ID | 64 kB, 4 kB, `0x1BB8202F` | Reported by the chip itself | measured | Read from the chip, 2026-10-06 |
| Build of TI's blink | 3.3 s | 32 MHz host build, 1 run | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `blink_build` |
| Flash with OpenOCD | 0.6 s | 1 run | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `blink_flash` (openocd) |
| Flash with UniFlash command line | 15.0 s | 1 run, `MSPM0L1306_ML130001.ccxml` | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `blink_flash` (uniflash) |
| Command to confirmed blink, `start.sh` | 75 s | Pin read through the debugger | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `time_to_blink` (oneline-terminal-start-sh) |
| Out-of-box image restored | all 64 kB of flash read back identical; demo answered over serial | Original image saved before the first flash | measured | Readback compare, 2026-10-06 |
| CoreMark, TI Arm Clang -O3, no operating system | 78.27 per second, 2.446 per MHz (-Os 47.35, -Oz 41.63) | Bare metal, 32 MHz | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `coremark` (ticlang-bare-o3, -os, -oz) |
| CoreMark at 4 MHz (no flash wait state) | 2.631 per MHz; the one wait state at 32 MHz costs 7% | Bare metal, -O3 | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `coremark_per_mhz` (ticlang-bare-o3-4mhz) |
| CoreMark under Zephyr, GCC -O2 with unrolling | 59.70 per second, 1.87 per MHz | Zephyr 4.4.2, 32 MHz | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `coremark` (gcc-zephyr-o2unroll); `zephyr/README.md` |
| Interrupt latency, pend to handler | 25 to 28 cycles bare metal; 119 to 137 through Zephyr | Pend a spare interrupt line | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `irq_latency` (bare, zephyr) |
| GPIO, one register write | 1 cycle | Not checked on a scope | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `gpio_toggle` (register) |
| Internal oscillator | 32.16 MHz, 0.5% fast (data sheet ±1.2%) | Measured on this bench | measured | Measured 2026-10-06 |
| ADC top rate, TI's example with DMA | 1.45 million samples per second | TI's 8-cycle window | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `adc_max_rate` |
| Room-occupancy neural nets | 500, 2k and 8k parameter models: 20 of 20 test vectors each; the 8k model in 84 to 100 ms | -O3 and -Os builds | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, tests `ai_occ_latency`, `ai_occ_fit` (occ_cnn_8k) |
| P-256 signature (micro-ecc, assembly) | sign 0.50 s, verify 0.57 s | 32 MHz | measured | `third-party/README.md` |
| Dhrystone 2.1, rules followed | 0.73 DMIPS/MHz (23.4 DMIPS); 0.88 at 4 MHz | 32 MHz | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `dhrystone` |
| FFT, 256 points, q15, TI's CMSIS-DSP | 2.25 ms; 512 points 5.2 ms | 32 MHz | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `fft256` (q15) |
| FreeRTOS (TI's V11.2.0, no TI example for this chip) | runs; task switch 12 to 16 µs; 11 small tasks fit | Static allocation | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, tests `rtos_task_switch`, `rtos_max_tasks`; `freertos/README.md` |
| ADC speed against accuracy | 1.99 Msps possible, but a sensor reads 10% low at that speed; TI's default window reads 1.7% low | Thermistor, window of 2 cycles against 8 | measured | Measured 2026-10-06 |
| UART loop, one jumper wire | every byte right to 4.5 Mbaud and from 6.4 to 10.67 Mbaud; 5 to 6 Mbaud fails, the same dead band as the MSPM0G3507 | Bytes compared after the loop | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `uart_max_clean` |
| Hardware CRC-32 against a lookup table | 10.9 times faster | 1 kB buffer | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `crc_speedup`; `third-party/README.md` |
| TI's SDK examples | 156 of 170 build from a terminal; all 148 that do not write the boot configuration were flashed and run by a script, low-power ones included: none crashed, the debugger never lost the board | MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07 | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, tests `examples_built`, `examples_ran_clean` |
| G3507 and C1104 examples retargeted to this chip | 133 built and ran, none crashed; 17 of the G3507 ones toggled an LED | Device changed in SysConfig | measured | `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, test `port_build_rate` |

No current or energy figures were taken in this README's run: TI's EnergyTrace software has no macOS version, and no other meter was on the bench for it. The later EnergyTrace rows are in the CSV.


## What fits in 4 kB and what does not

| Program | RAM it needs | Fits? |
|---|--:|---|
| TI's blink example | 256 B | yes |
| Every TI SDK example that builds | up to 3.2 kB | yes |
| CoreMark (standard 2 kB data), bare metal | 3.9 kB | yes, 144 B spare; the stack reached 2.9 kB |
| Room-occupancy model, 8k parameters | 2.2 kB plus 548 B of stack | yes |
| Room-occupancy model, 30k parameters | over 4 kB for its buffers alone | no |
| FreeRTOS, one-task blink (static allocation) | 1.0 kB | yes, 3.0 kB spare |
| FreeRTOS with TI's own settings file for this board | 5.4 kB | no |
| Zephyr hello_world | 3.7 kB | yes, 264 B spare |
| Zephyr CoreMark (2 kB data) | 4.0 kB | yes, after turning off the C library heap |
| Zephyr synchronization, logger, shell, philosophers, as shipped | 6.1 to 17.0 kB | no |
| Zephyr shell (minimal), logger, synchronization, Thread-Metric, trimmed | up to 4.0 kB | yes, all ran; the shell has 48 B left |
| Embench: 14 of 19 fit and run, 13 pass | | yes |
| Embench: heatshrink, huffbench, matmult-int, qrduino, sglib-combined | 6.9 to 8.5 kB | no |
| Embench: wikisort | 4.1 kB of stack in one function | no: it links, then faults at run time |

Flash was never the limit; the largest image, the Zephyr benchmark at its O3 setting, used 54.9 kB of 64 kB (`zephyr/README.md`).

## Compared with the other TI boards on this bench

Measured means run on this board; data sheet means read, not run.

| LP-MSPM0G3507 | LP-EM-CC2340R5 | LP-CC1354P10-1 | LP-MSPM0L1306 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Core, clock | Cortex-M0+, 80 MHz | Cortex-M0+, 48 MHz | Cortex-M33 with FPU, 48 MHz (data sheet) | Cortex-M0+, 32 MHz |
| Flash, RAM | 128 kB, 32 kB | 512 kB, 36 kB | 1 MB, 256 kB (data sheet) | 64 kB, 4 kB |
| Extra hardware | math accelerator, AES, CRC, random numbers | AES (data sheet) | AES, random numbers (data sheet) | CRC, op-amps, comparator |
| Radio | none | Bluetooth LE, Zigbee; Thread only as a radio co-processor | Sub-1 GHz and 2.4 GHz | none |
| CoreMark, TI Clang -O3, bare metal | 183.61 (2.30 per MHz; 2.46 at 32 MHz) | 111.09 (2.31) | not measured | 78.27 (2.446) |
| CoreMark, Zephyr GCC -O2 with unrolling | 139.88 (1.75) | 84.07 (1.75) | no Zephyr support | 59.70 (1.87) |
| Interrupt latency, bare metal | 29 to 36 cycles | 28 to 29 | not measured | 25 to 28 |
| Hardware CRC-32 against a table | 13.5 times | not measured | not measured | 10.9 times |
| Zephyr board in upstream 4.4.2 | yes | yes, no radio | no | no; chip yes, the board file in this repo works |
| TI SDK examples | 270 (13 Edge AI, TI Drivers, FreeRTOS) | F3 SDK, TI Drivers, FreeRTOS | F2 SDK, not installed here | 170, DriverLib only; FreeRTOS runs with this repo's settings |

The three Cortex-M0+ parts have the same core speed per MHz with the same compiler. The L1306 even needs fewer cycles than the G3507 for the same code (CoreMark 1.87 against 1.75 per MHz under Zephyr; Embench 0.93 times the G3507's cycles), because at 32 MHz its flash adds one wait state and the G3507's adds two at 80 MHz. What separates them is clock, RAM and the extra hardware. The L1306 is the cheapest by far and the one where every program has to be sized for RAM first. Sources: the other boards' rows in `data/results/`, the CC1354P10 page `../cc1354p10/README.md`, and ti.com for prices.

## Moving code to and from it

- **Plain C moves.** CoreMark, Embench, micro-ecc, jsmn and the occupancy models built and ran with board code only (clock, UART pins, stack size). The prebuilt model libraries made for the G3507 ran unchanged and gave the same answers on all 20 test vectors; the Zephyr benchmark's neural-net checksums match the G3507's and the CC2340R5's.
- **TI's own examples move up easily and down badly.** Changing only the device in SysConfig: 101 of 170 L1306 examples build for the G3507, but only 22 of 270 G3507 examples build for the L1306. The single biggest blocker is one G-series SysConfig setting (`SYSCTL.forceDefaultClkConfig`) that the L1306 does not have; SysConfig's command line stops on it. Dropping every line SysConfig rejects gets 96 of 270 to build, and 13 of those silently lose a real setting, such as the ADC's DMA trigger. All 133 ported images that built ran on the board with no crash, but running is not the same as working. A C1104 blink moved this way still toggles the C1104 kit's LED pin, PA22, which on this board is wired to the light sensor; and dropped settings change behavior.
- **One TI example ported by hand.** The G3507's internal temperature example needs four SysConfig lines changed and no C changes. SysConfig picks the software IQmath library by itself.
- **Interrupt lines are a trap.** This chip's interrupt controller implements only the 13 lines that have a peripheral; pending any other line does nothing, silently. Code that borrows an unused line on the G3507 (the test used line 28) breaks here.

## Problems found

Each one is in the [FAQ](FAQ.md) with the fix.

- The internal temperature sensor reads -165 °C with this chip's factory calibration. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: wrong factory trim).** A TI forum answer says early samples carry a wrong trim.
- CCStudio 21.0.1's notes for AI agents (`ai/boards/LP-MSPM0L1306/AGENTS.md`) list the package as LQFP-32, the BoosterPack header pins as differing from the LaunchPad user guide's figure, and ADC channels 7 and 8 on PA19 and PA18. The user guide (SLAU869E) and data sheet (SLASEX0D) give VQFN-32 (RHB) and PA18 and PA16. Take pin and channel numbers from the user guide's BoosterPack figure.
- The out-of-box demo's GUI needs a request to TI sales; the demo's serial protocol is only in its source. **Tag: Tool or docs.**
- Zephyr: the GPIO driver does not compile for this chip (`'IOMUX_PINCM38' undeclared`) and there is no pin-mux file. **Tag: Third-party behavior.**
- Zephyr: every program that filled RAM stopped at `***** HARD FAULT *****` during boot, because the C library heap defaults to all RAM left over. **Tag: Third-party behavior.**
- The 30k-parameter model fails to link on RAM (`program will not fit into available memory`). **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).**
- 14 of 170 SDK examples do not build from a terminal: no makefile, a TI build-server path, or `symbol "interruptVectors" redefined`. **Tag: Tool or docs.**
- Embench `st` fails its own check, as on the G3507. **Tag: Third-party behavior.**
- A SysConfig clock line is ignored without a warning when the clock tree is on. **Tag: Tool or docs.**

## If you see this

- If you see `wrong # args: should be "error message ?stacktrace?"` after `mspm0_mass_erase`, ignore it and load an image with DSLite or OpenOCD: the script's reset helper throws after the erase has happened.
- If you see `DAP Connection Error. This could be caused by the device having gone to low power mode.`, the image entered SHUTDOWN right after boot. Hold S1 (PA18), press and release S3, keep S1 held 2 more seconds, then flash a non-sleeping image at once and replug USB.
- If you see `error: 'IOMUX_PINCM38' undeclared here (not in a function)` building Zephyr, build with the out-of-tree board in `zephyr/` (`-DBOARD_ROOT`): Zephyr 4.4.2's GPIO driver has the 80-pin MSPM0L222x pin table.

The rest, each with cause and fix, are in [FAQ.md](FAQ.md).

## Where these facts come from

Checked 2026-10-06 on an Intel Mac, macOS 15.7.9: MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07, TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS (from CCStudio 21.0.1), SysConfig 1.26.3, xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0+dev, UniFlash 9.6.0, Zephyr 4.4.2 with GCC 12.2.0. One LP-MSPM0L1306, onboard XDS110 probe serial <probe serial>, firmware 3.0.0.43, powered and flashed over its USB cable. No jumper or wire was changed, except the one jumper wire of the UART loop test.

Files: `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`, `AGENTS.md`, `FAQ.md`.

==============================================================================
FILE: mspm0l1306/FAQ.md | TI LP-MSPM0L1306 LaunchPad on a Mac: errors and fixes
==============================================================================

# TI LP-MSPM0L1306 LaunchPad on a Mac: errors and fixes

Every problem hit bringing up the TI LP-MSPM0L1306 LaunchPad (MSPM0L1306 chip: Arm Cortex-M0+, 32 MHz, 64 kB flash, 4 kB RAM; onboard XDS110 probe) from a Mac terminal on 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07. Each answer starts with the fix, names what caused it, and quotes the exact error text so a search finds it. Versions: Intel Mac, macOS 15.7.9, MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07, TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS, SysConfig 1.26.3, UniFlash 9.6.0, xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0+dev, Zephyr 4.4.2 with GCC 12.2.0.

**What caused it**, one tag per answer:

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Our mistake | A mistake in this repo's runs. Listed so you do not repeat it |
| Setup or handling | How the hardware was plugged in or set up |
| TI example default | A TI example's default works on TI's bench but not for this job |
| Tool or docs | A TI tool bug, a missing tool, or a missing or wrong instruction |
| Chip limit | The silicon cannot do it, usually RAM |
| Third-party behavior | Upstream Zephyr, OpenOCD, macOS or open-source code, not TI |
| Unknown | Not found |

Contents: [Setting up CCStudio and the AI on a Mac](#setting-up-ccstudio-and-the-ai-on-a-mac), [Connecting and flashing](#connecting-and-flashing), [Memory](#memory), [Analog and sensors](#analog-and-sensors), [Zephyr](#zephyr), [Building and moving code](#building-and-moving-code), [DriverLib, TI Drivers and Zephyr](#driverlib-ti-drivers-and-zephyr).

Words used below (more in [docs/vocab.md](../docs/vocab.md)): the **probe** is the XDS110 debugger built into the LaunchPad; it shows up on the Mac as two serial ports, `/dev/cu.usbmodem<serial>1` (the board's UART) and `...4`. **OpenOCD** is an open-source flashing and debug tool. **NONMAIN** is the chip's boot configuration area at 0x41C00000. 1 kB = 1,024 bytes.

## The one-command route (`./start.sh` and `tools/frl`)

Checked on 2026-10-14 on an Intel Mac with this board, MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07, SysConfig 1.26.3, TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS and xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7. The route itself is in [docs/frl.md](../docs/frl.md); every code is in [docs/frl-errors.md](../docs/frl-errors.md).

### Do I need an AI account or CCStudio to blink a pattern on the LP-MSPM0L1306?

No. `./start.sh mspm0l1306 blink --probe <serial> --pattern 150,150,150,900` builds, flashes and checks it with TI's SDK, SysConfig, compiler and xPack OpenOCD, no assistant and no CCStudio window; about 13 s of machine time on this bench. An assistant is optional (`--assistant claude` or `codex`). **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### `./start.sh` says "FRL-E001 REFUSED: no XDS110 debug probe found on USB". The board's light is on. Why?

The cable is most likely charge-only, or it is in the wrong connector. Use a USB data cable in the connector on the top half of the board (the XDS110 debugger), straight into the computer. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### It says "FRL-E002 REFUSED: 2 probes on USB". Which one is my board?

Run `python3 tools/frl/frl.py detect`, unplug the other board, run it again: the serial that stays is this board. Pass it with `--probe`. The tool never picks one by order. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### It says "FRL-E004 ... could not be opened; another program (CCStudio, UniFlash or another OpenOCD) may hold it". What do I close?

CCStudio's or UniFlash's debug connection on this board, or another terminal still running OpenOCD. If the message names another frl run instead ("in use by ... run ..."), wait for it to finish. The tool never stops them itself. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### It says "FRL-E006 FAILED: OpenOCD could not attach to the board" with "DAP Connection Error. This could be caused by the device having gone to low power mode." What now?

The program on the chip sleeps right after starting. Hold S1 (PA18), press and release S3 (reset), keep S1 held 2 more seconds, then at once run `./start.sh` again, which flashes the blink program; unplug and replug USB afterwards. If there is no low-power line, check all nine J101 jumpers are on. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### It says "FRL-E021 REFUSED: sysconfig 1.28.0 installed; this route was validated with 1.26.3". Must I install another SysConfig?

Either install 1.26.3, or keep yours and name it: `export FRL_SYSCONFIG=/Applications/ti/sysconfig_1.28.0`. The run is then recorded as unvalidated. The same code with "has no target/ti_mspm0.cfg" means the OpenOCD found is too old (Homebrew's 0.12.0): install xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7. **Tag: Tool or docs.**

### It says "FRL-E070 REFUSED: the project folder ... has a space in its path". Why can't it build there?

TI's example makefile passes generated option files unquoted, so a space splits the path (`tiarmclang: error: no such file or directory: '@é/ticlang/device.opt'` for a folder named `my blink é`). Set `FRL_PROJECTS` to a folder with no spaces. The same code also refuses a pattern outside the limits: each time 50 to 5,000 ms, at most 8 on/off pairs, one cycle at most 6 s. **Tag: Tool or docs.**

### It says "FRL-E040 FAILED: LED2 red (PA26) does not follow the asked pattern". The build and flash passed. What is on the board?

Suspected: another program than the one just built, for example because the flash step did not run or a different board was flashed. The message says what the LED did. Run the same `./start.sh` command again; it rebuilds, flashes and checks. TI's unchanged blink shows "on 498, off 497" here. **Tag: Unknown.**

### `./start.sh mspm0l1306 print-a-message` says "FRL-E040 FAILED: nothing arrived on /dev/cu.usbmodem...1". Why is the port silent?

J16 and J17 are probably on BP (left), which sends the UART to the header pins instead of the USB port. Move both to XDS (right, as shipped) and run the command again. Another program holding the serial port (a terminal, CCStudio's serial view) can also take the bytes first. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### Can Codex, the ChatGPT app or Claude Code flash my LP-MSPM0L1306 for me?

Yes, from the computer the board is plugged into, through the same local tool. The Codex command-line tool that comes inside the ChatGPT app backed up, built, flashed and checked the board in 56 s; Claude Code did the same through `./start.sh --assistant claude` in 92 s, and the check passed both times. Nobody has done it from an app's own chat window; docs/frl-desktop-apps.md has the setup. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### Does the route work on Linux?

Building does: in an Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 container, emulated on an Apple Silicon Mac, with TI's Linux installers for TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS and SysConfig 1.28.1 (no login) and the MSPM0 SDK copied from a Mac (its download needs a myTI login), `frl build` made the image in 3.9 s, and that image passed the check on this board. SysConfig 1.28.1 is not the tested 1.26.3, so set `FRL_SYSCONFIG` and the run is recorded as unvalidated. Flashing from Linux is untested (no board on that computer). **Tag: Tool or docs.**

### Do I have to pass `--probe` with only one board plugged in?

No: with exactly one XDS110 on USB the tool uses it. With two or more it stops (`FRL-E002`) until you name one. The single-board case passed this repo's tests with simulated hardware; every run on the real bench had several boards and named the probe. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### `print-a-message` refuses my text with "FRL-E070 REFUSED: use plain letters, digits, spaces and punctuation, without quotes or backslashes". What may the message contain?

1 to 40 plain characters: letters, digits, spaces and punctuation, but no quotes or backslashes, because the text goes into a C string in TI's example. **Tag: Tool or docs.**

### On Windows, `print-a-message` ends "not verified". Did it work?

Maybe: the tool does not look for the serial port on Windows (`FRL-E042 ... could not find the serial port ... on this OS (untested here)`). Open the board's first USB serial port at 115200 baud in a terminal program and look for your message. **Tag: Tool or docs.**

### How do I share what went wrong without sharing my computer's details?

Run `python3 tools/frl/frl.py status --report`. It prints the last run's summary with your home folder, user and computer name and IP addresses removed, and the probe serial shortened to its last two characters. Read it before you paste it anywhere; the tool sends nothing. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### A desktop app's `frl_verify` or `frl_flash` call fails asking for `probe`. Why, with one board plugged in?

The tools that read or write a board through an app (`frl_backup`, `frl_verify`, `frl_verify_image`, `frl_flash`, `frl_restore`) always need the probe serial named, so an app never picks a board on its own. Call `frl_detect` first and pass the serial it lists. **Tag: Tool or docs.**

### How do I put TI's out-of-box demo back after using `./start.sh`?

`python3 tools/frl/frl.py restore "<first backup folder>" --probe <serial>`. The first backup holds the demo the board shipped with; later runs back up whatever was on the board then. Restore writes main flash, reads it back and compares; it ran five times on this bench, each with a match. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### Does the route work on an Apple Silicon Mac?

Building does: on an Apple Silicon Mac (macOS 26.3) with TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS for arm64, SysConfig 1.28.1 (it runs under Rosetta) and xPack OpenOCD for arm64, `frl build` made the image in 14.7 s, and that image passed the check on this board. Flashing from an Apple Silicon Mac is untested, and SysConfig 1.28.1 is not the tested 1.26.3, so set `FRL_SYSCONFIG` and the run is recorded as unvalidated. **Tag: Tool or docs.**

### Codex says "MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never". Is the tool broken?

No. Codex refuses tools that write the board when it cannot ask you. Run it interactively, or approve the one tool for that run (`-c 'mcp_servers.frl.tools.frl_flash.approval_mode="approve"'`). If Codex sits at "Reading additional input from stdin...", start it with `< /dev/null`. Details: docs/frl-desktop-apps.md. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### A desktop app's `frl_host` reports a Linux VM or 0 probes. Can it reach the board?

No: that app runs the tool somewhere without your USB devices (a cloud run or a VM). Run `./start.sh` in a terminal on the computer with the board, and use the app to read and explain. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### It says "FRL-E020 REFUSED: ... missing: mspm0_sdk not found; sysconfig not found; ...". What do I install?

Run `python3 tools/frl/frl.py doctor --board mspm0l1306`: it lists every missing tool with its download link and size (MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07, SysConfig 1.26.3, TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS, xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7). Install them, or point to copies elsewhere with `FRL_MSPM0_SDK`, `FRL_SYSCONFIG`, `FRL_TICLANG` or `FRL_OPENOCD`. Have about 12 GB free if the compiler comes with CCStudio. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### macOS refuses to open the xPack OpenOCD because it was downloaded from the internet. How do I run it?

Clear the download flag once: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/xpack-openocd-0.12.0-7`. The exact wording of macOS's warning differs between versions; it did not appear on the Mac used here, where OpenOCD came with the Zephyr toolchain. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### Claude Desktop cannot connect to the Fox Red Labs extension; its log says "Couldn't start for Cowork and Code sessions. Error: Connection closed". What do I do?

Open the extension's log, `~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp-server-Fox Red Labs host check.log` on a Mac (on Windows: not run): the lines under that error say why the server stopped. Check that `python3 --version` prints 3.9 or later, then remove the extension and install the newest `.mcpb` (`python3 tools/frl/cowork/build_mcpb.py <folder>` builds it). **Tag: Unknown.** The current build asks for no folder and should start. If it still fails this way, include the log's last lines in a report. Details: docs/frl-desktop-apps.md.

### `make` or `python3` is not found on my Mac. What do I install?

Apple's command line tools: `xcode-select --install`. They bring `make` and Python 3.9, which the route needs. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### A desktop app lists no frl tools. What is wrong?

The app cannot start the server. Its log says why: on a Mac, `~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp-server-<extension name>.log` for Claude Desktop. Check `python3 --version` prints 3.9 or later, and reinstall the newest extension; the current ones carry the tool and ask no questions. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### The assistant says it is done, but the check failed. Which do I believe?

The check. It read the board; the assistant's words did not. The message says what the LED did, and `python3 tools/frl/frl.py status --handoff` gives a summary to continue from. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

### Can Claude's Cowork reach my board?

Anthropic's Cowork architecture page says local MCP servers do not run in cloud runs. Install the read-only `frl-hostcheck.mcpb` first (`python3 tools/frl/cowork/build_mcpb.py <folder>` builds it) and ask a new Cowork run to call `frl_host`; if it reports this computer and your probe count, the board tools can work there. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

## Connecting and flashing

### OpenOCD says "Could not find MEM-AP to control the core" and DSLite says "Peripheral mis-configuration (e.g improper watchdog or clock)". The chip resets itself in a loop. How do I get back in?

Mass-erase it through the debug mailbox, which works while the core is unreachable. **Tag: Setup or handling.** Cause: a window-watchdog example that refreshed the watchdog inside the closed window, and the chip reset every few milliseconds from the first boot. The command that recovered it, with xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7: `openocd -f interface/xds110.cfg -c "adapter serial ML130001" -f target/ti_mspm0.cfg -c "mspm0x.cpu configure -defer-examine" -c init -c mspm0_mass_erase -c shutdown`. The script then throws `wrong # args: should be "error message ?stacktrace?"` from its reset helper; the erase has already happened and the next DSLite load works. Without a terminal: hold S1 while pressing S3 to enter the bootloader. The port that hit it is `ports/cms32/README.md`.

### Will a low-power example knock the LP-MSPM0L1306 off the debugger, as it did the MSPM0G3507?

Not in the runs made here. **Tag: Unknown.** All 13 of TI's low-power, watchdog and flash-protection examples for this board (12 STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN and watchdog examples plus `flashctl_dynamic_memory_protection`), and 9 more whose SysConfig selects STOP or STANDBY, were flashed and run by a script, and the debugger reconnected every time. On the LP-MSPM0G3507 the same script lost the board twice and needed a USB replug. Each run started with a system reset that keeps the debugger attached, which may stop the chip from fully entering the deep modes; no meter was available to check. If you lose the board, unplug and replug its USB cable.

### What is the quickest way to flash the LP-MSPM0L1306 from a Mac terminal?

OpenOCD with its MSPM0 script, choosing the probe by serial number: a 440-byte blink took 0.6 seconds to program and verify. **Tag: Tool or docs.** No TI command-line tool writes the connection file its own flasher needs. TI's own command-line flasher (UniFlash's `dslite.sh`) also works but took 15.0 seconds for the same image, and it needs a connection file (`.ccxml`) that no TI command-line tool writes; the file used here is the G3507 file with two names changed (`MSPM0L1306_ML130001.ccxml`). The OpenOCD wrapper is `tools/ocd.sh`.

### OpenOCD prints "Error: checksum mismatch - attempting binary compare". Did the flash fail?

No. The next line, `** Verified OK **`, is the real result. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** OpenOCD's quick checksum check fails on every MSPM0 image flashed here, on this board and the LP-MSPM0G3507, and it falls back to reading the image back, which passes.

### OpenOCD says "Unable to reset target", then every connection fails with "Could not find MEM-AP to control the core". Is the chip dead?

No. With main flash blank, the chip's boot ROM keeps the debugger off the CPU after a reset. Connect, run TI's `mspm0_mass_erase` (it halts the CPU), then `flash write_image erase <file> 0x0 bin` with no reset, then `mspm0_board_reset`. **Tag: Our mistake.** Cause: on an MSPM0G3507, all of main flash was erased before OpenOCD's `program`, which resets first; `program` erases what it needs on its own. `mspm0_mass_erase` erases main flash only, not the boot configuration.

### Why does my program restart every time I connect the debugger?

OpenOCD's `init` resets the MSPM0 target, so each new connection starts the program again; the serial port shows the boot text twice. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** Read results in the same OpenOCD connection that started the program, or leave the program alone and use the serial port.

### The board came with a program on it. What is it, and can I get it back?

It is TI's out-of-box demo (`examples/nortos/LP_MSPM0L1306/demos/out_of_box`), built with an older toolchain than today's SDK: 9.5 kB, against 9.6 kB from SDK 2.11. **Tag: Setup or handling.** Save it before you flash anything: `tools/ocd.sh "dump_image flash-as-received.bin 0x0 0x10000"`. The copy from this board is in `data/out-of-box-as-received.bin` and restores with `tools/ocd.sh "reset halt" "program data/out-of-box-as-received.bin 0x0 verify" "reset run"`.

### The out-of-box demo is silent on the serial port. Is it broken?

No. It answers commands and sends nothing until asked. Send a MessagePack map ending in a newline, at 115200 baud, for example the bytes `81 AB 6C 69 67 68 74 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 C3 0A` (`{"lightEnable": true}`). It then streams `lsADC` light readings; `{"thermEnable": true}` streams `thADC`, the board temperature in degrees Celsius times 32. **Tag: Tool or docs.** The README points to a GUI and says "Please contact your local sales representative or TI support team to request access to the GUI." The message format is only in the source (`MSP_GUI/GUI_mpack.c`). Without the newline the demo ignores the message.

## Memory

### Why does my program print garbage at the end, or fault, on a 4 kB chip?

Check the stack size. TI's examples for this chip reserve 256 bytes of stack, and `printf("%f")` alone needs more than 400. **Tag: TI example default.** The CoreMark build passed its own checks while its final `printf` ran 148 bytes past a 2.8 kB stack and overwrote the end of the result text, with no fault. The chip has no memory protection unit, so nothing stops an overflow. Fill RAM with a pattern before running and look for the lowest overwritten word (`tools/paintrun.sh`), and set the stack in the linker file (`--stack_size`).

### Embench's wikisort builds for this chip and then never finishes. Why?

Its main function reserves 4.1 kB of stack in one instruction, more than the chip's 4 kB of RAM. **Tag: Chip limit.** That is the benchmark as written, at -O2 and -Os. The stack pointer lands below RAM (0x1FFFFEE0) and the first write faults into the default handler. The linker cannot see this; only a run does. `third-party/README.md`.

### Which of the room-occupancy neural nets fit?

The 500, 2k and 8k parameter models run, 20 of 20 test vectors each, the 8k one in 84 to 100 ms at 32 MHz. The 30k model does not link: `program will not fit into available memory` for `.bss`. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** Its buffers alone need more than 4 kB as generated; reusing buffers between layers was not run.

## Analog and sensors

### Why does the internal temperature sensor read about -165 °C?

The factory calibration word on the chip tested (`TEMP_SENSE0` at 0x41C4003C, 369) does not match its sensor. With the typical value from TI's manual instead, the same reading gives about 21.7 °C, and the board's thermistor read 22.8 °C. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: wrong factory trim).** A public TI forum thread (E2E 1311550) reports the same impossible result on LP-MSPM0L1306 boards, and TI's answer there is that early samples carry a wrong temperature trim. Whether this chip is an early sample is not confirmed. Use the onboard thermistor (PA15, ADC channel 9) or calibrate against a known temperature.

### Is there an internal temperature sensor example for the L1306?

No. Only the G-series has one (`adc12_internal_temp_sensor_mathacl`), and it uses the G-series math accelerator. **Tag: Tool or docs.** It ports with four SysConfig changes and no C changes: device and package lines, board line, `genLibIQVersion` from `MATHACL` to `RTS`, and remove `SYSCTL.forceDefaultClkConfig`.

### Why does TI's "max frequency" ADC example reach 1.45 million samples per second when the data sheet says 1.68?

Its 8-cycle sample window sets the rate. With 4 cycles it does 1.77 million and with 2 cycles 1.99 million, but on the board's thermistor every shorter window reads lower: 1.7% low at TI's 8 cycles, 5.3% at 4, 9.9% at 2, against a 64-cycle reading. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** The input must settle onto the sampling capacitor; the sensor's source impedance was not measured and no buffered input was tried. Use a longer window for sensors, or buffer the input with an op-amp..

### I changed the clock in SysConfig and nothing changed. Why?

If the file has `SYSCTL.clockTreeEn = true`, the clock tree setting wins: `system.clockTree["SYSOSC"].frequencySelect = 4` sets 4 MHz, and `SYSCTL.SYSOSC_Freq = 4000000` alone is ignored with no warning. **Tag: Tool or docs.** After any clock change, read `CPUCLK_FREQ` in the generated `ti_msp_dl_config.h`.

### Why does my UART return garbage at 5 to 6 Mbaud on the LP-MSPM0L1306?

The UART fails between 5 and 6 Mbaud at 32 MHz with TI's DriverLib baud setup and works on both sides of that band; other clocks were not tested. In a loop test (PA8 wired to PA9, 2 kB of random bytes per speed, 2026-10-06) every byte came back right from 9,600 baud to 4.5 Mbaud and from 6.4 to 10.67 Mbaud; 5 Mbaud got 38 right, 5.33 Mbaud 1 to 5, 5.5 Mbaud 178, 6 Mbaud 94%, with framing, break and overrun flags (`RXDATA` bits `0x100`, `0x400`, `0x800`). The LP-MSPM0G3507 gives nearly the same counts. At 12 Mbaud DriverLib sets a divisor of 0 and nothing is sent, with no error. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs).** Neither chip's errata (SLAZ742H, SLAZ741D) lists it, and the UART block was not separated from DriverLib's setup. Stay at or below 4.5 Mbaud, or test your exact speed first. Detail: `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`.

### I wired PA8 to PA9 for the UART loop and nothing comes back. Why?

Move jumpers J16 and J17 to the BP side (left) first, then wire J1 pin 4 (PA8) to J1 pin 3 (PA9). **Tag: Tool or docs.** Out of the box those two jumpers route the chip's UART to the debugger's USB serial port, so a wire on the header connects to nothing; TI's loopback example README does not mention them. Move them back to XDS (right) afterwards or the board's serial window stays silent.

## Zephyr

### Does Zephyr support the LP-MSPM0L1306?

Zephyr 4.4.2 has the chip but no board for this LaunchPad. The out-of-tree board in this repo (`zephyr/boards/ti/lp_mspm0l1306/`) runs hello_world and blinky. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** Zephyr's own GPIO driver does not compile for this chip and there is no pin-mux file for the MSPM0L130x family; both are worked around in the board folder. `zephyr/README.md`.

### Zephyr's blinky fails with "error: 'IOMUX_PINCM38' undeclared here (not in a function)". Why?

Zephyr 4.4.2's MSPM0 GPIO driver has the pin table of the 80-pin MSPM0L222x, and this 32-pin chip has no `IOMUX_PINCM38` to `PINCM74`. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** Use the corrected copy of the driver in this repo's board folder (`zephyr/boards/ti/lp_mspm0l1306/`), which keeps only the pins this chip has.

### Every Zephyr program that fills RAM stops at boot with "***** HARD FAULT *****". Why?

Set `CONFIG_COMMON_LIBC_MALLOC_ARENA_SIZE=0` if the program does not call `malloc`. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** Zephyr's C library heap defaults to all RAM left after the program. With 8 to 16 bytes left, setting up the heap writes past the end of RAM: the fault address was in `sys_heap_init`, called from `malloc_prepare`. Nothing warns at build time.

### My interrupt test works on the MSPM0G3507 but the handler never runs on the L1306. Why?

Use an interrupt line that has a peripheral on this chip. **Tag: Chip limit.** The L1306 implements only lines 0, 1, 2, 4, 9, 13, 15, 16, 18, 20, 24, 25 and 31 (the enable register reads back `0x8315a217` after writing all ones). Pending any other line does nothing, and neither CMSIS nor Zephyr's `IRQ_CONNECT` complains. The test had borrowed line 28, which is AES on the G3507; line 25 (I2C1, unused) works.

### Why does a Zephyr "-O3" build run at -O2?

Put the optimisation flag on the file itself with a per-file compile option. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** Zephyr adds its own `-O2` after the application's flags, and GCC uses the last one, so a project-wide `-O3` is overridden (and loop unrolling stays on). `zephyr/README.md` shows the per-file option.

### Why does a Zephyr sample fail with "region `RAM' overflowed"?

As shipped, most do: synchronization needs 6.1 kB, logger 8 kB, shell_module 12.5 kB and philosophers 17 kB, mostly in stacks (Zephyr's interrupt stack alone defaults to 2 kB). **Tag: Third-party behavior.** That is Zephyr's sample defaults, not the chip: with stacks and buffers cut, the shell (minimal setting, 48 bytes left), the logger in both modes, synchronization and all eight Thread-Metric tests ran on the board. philosophers was not run. The exact settings are in `zephyr/extra/README.md`.

## Building and moving code

### Do Cmsemicon's CMS32F04x example programs run on the LP-MSPM0L1306?

34 of the 53 variants in Cmsemicon's Keil pack build and ran on this board on 2026-10-07, 29 with their `main.c` unchanged, through a glue layer of 845 lines of C that implements Cmsemicon's function names on DriverLib. Of the 19 not built, 7 need CAN, a segment LCD, USB fast charge or a clock monitor the L1306 does not have. **Tag: Chip limit.** The other 12 are I2C and SPI examples that need a second device on the bench. **Tag: Setup or handling.** Two more things to know: the temperature-sensor example prints a wrong temperature because the glue's trim constants are placeholders, and the flash example's 512-byte pages land on the L1306's 1 kB sectors, so two of its erases wipe a neighbour it just wrote (both **Tag: Setup or handling**, detail on the port page). Detail and the per-example record: `ports/cms32/README.md`.

### My ported example's LED never blinks, but the same code blinks at -O0. Why?

The example polls a plain global (`extern uint32_t g_ticks`) that an interrupt decrements, without `volatile`, so at -O2 the compiler turns the wait into an endless branch. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** Cmsemicon's Keil projects build at optimization level 0, which hides it. Build that file at -O0, or add `volatile`. Seen with TI Arm Clang 5.1.1 on 2026-10-07, `ports/cms32/README.md`.

### Some SDK examples for the L1306 will not build from the terminal. Which, and why?

14 of 170. **Tag: Tool or docs.** 9 have no makefile (CCStudio project only), 2 have a path from TI's build server in their makefile (`/home/developer/.cache/bazel/...`: `dali_led_demo`, `drv8329aevm_gui_firmware`), and the three `bsl_software_invoke_app_demo_*` stop at link with `symbol "interruptVectors" redefined`. None fails to compile.

### I moved an MSPM0C1104 example to the L1306 by changing the device in SysConfig. It runs, but the LED does not blink. Why?

It is blinking a pin with no LED. Unlock the pin assignments, or set the LED pin by hand (PA0 red, PA26, PA13 and PA27 for the RGB LED). **Tag: Tool or docs.** Changing the device keeps the old board's pins: the ported `gpio_toggle_output` toggled PA22 and PA2, the C1104 kit's LED and test pins, and on this board PA22 is the light sensor's amplifier output. SysConfig gives no warning. With the assignments removed it picked PA0, the red LED.

### Does FreeRTOS run on the LP-MSPM0L1306? TI's settings file will not link

Yes, with static allocation and smaller stacks: a one-task blink uses 1 kB of RAM, 11 small tasks fit, and a task switch takes 12 to 16 microseconds. **Tag: TI example default.** TI ships no FreeRTOS example for this chip, and its `kernel/freertos/builds/LP_MSPM0L1306/release/FreeRTOSConfig.h` sets a 3 kB heap and 512-byte task stacks, which needs 5.4 kB of zero-filled RAM on a 4 kB chip. Settings and build: `freertos/README.md`.

### Why is there no Trace or EnergyTrace item in CCStudio 21 on my Mac? Can I measure current on the LP-MSPM0L1306 from a Mac?

Not in CCStudio 21.0.1 as installed. Two functions in the IDE's own code return "not supported" on macOS (the comment says "not supported on Mac OS, only windows and linux"), so the Run, Trace menu is hidden. **Tag: Tool or docs.** Behind that switch, TI's Mac trace server library fails to load with `Library not loaded: @rpath/libti_logger.dylib` (it ships with a build-server path and a Linux-style search path) and the capture library, loaded on its own, with `Library not loaded: @rpath/libxdsfast3.dylib`. **Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs).** It cannot see the probe driver folder by itself; the debugger may load it differently. With the switch removed and three library paths corrected in copies placed in a mirror of the install tree (the install itself was not changed), the three libraries tested (`libCloudTrace`, `libenergytraceccs`, `libTraceFactory`) load; the other 72 in that folder were not tested. The IDE path then dies anyway: the Mac DSLite answers `Unknown sub module: "trace"`. **Tag: Tool or docs.** So the capture runs without the IDE: `tools/energytrace/etcap.py` talks to the probe through CCStudio's XDS110 driver library and gives the numbers in `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`. Apple silicon was not tested (the files checked are Intel builds). TI's command-line capture tool `stune` is documented for Windows only and is not in the Mac install. Two more libraries in `ccs_base/common/bin` carry the same Linux-style search path, and the five files checked (the three patched libraries, DSLite and the app) are not code-signed, so the patch is expected not to trip macOS library validation. TI's answer on E2E is CCStudio 12.8, whose last supported macOS is Ventura (TI staff, E2E thread 1579854), and TI's tracker entry EXT_EP-12168 (open since 2025-01) gives "Use CCS 12.x" as the workaround. To measure today: `python3 tools/energytrace/etcap.py --serial ML130001 --seconds 20 --csv out.csv`, or a meter across the J101 3V3 jumper (user's guide section 2.6). Detail and the patch: `docs/experiments/2026-10-06-mac-energytrace-ccstudio.md`.

### My sleep-current reading never drops below about 2.6 mA, whatever power mode I set. Why?

A debugger has been attached since the last power-on reset. The debug subsystem stays enabled until a power-on reset, and while it is enabled the chip stays in SLEEP0 whatever policy the code sets. **Tag: Setup or handling.** Make the program check the reset cause on boot and trigger one software power-on reset (the deep-sleep test image does), or unplug and replug the board. After that OpenOCD cannot reach the sleeping chip ("Debug AP not available"); DSLite can: `DSLite flash -c mspm0l1306/MSPM0L1306_ML130001.ccxml -f -v <file.out>`. Numbers:

### After flashing a SHUTDOWN test, nothing can connect: "DAP Connection Error. This could be caused by the device having gone to low power mode." Is the board bricked?

No, but it is locked out. A program that enters SHUTDOWN right after boot runs back into it on every reset, before any debugger can attach. **Tag: Our mistake.** OpenOCD's mailbox mass erase did not reach it either (OpenOCD exits as soon as the debug port fails to answer). What worked: hold S1 (the bootloader button, PA18) while pressing and releasing S3 (reset), keep S1 held two more seconds; the chip sits in TI's bootloader with its debug port alive, and OpenOCD attaches within a second. After that rescue the chip kept starting in the ROM bootloader at every debugger reset until a plain USB power cycle (seen on a later use of the board); unplug and replug once the new image is on. Flash any non-sleeping image at once. Prevention: every deep-sleep image waits 3 s at boot.

### EnergyTrace reads 1.5 mA with the chip in SHUTDOWN, where the data sheet says 61 nA. Is the tool wrong?

No. A pin is. The test image drives PA1 low, and the LaunchPad pulls PA1 up to 3.3 V through 2,200 Ω when jumper J10 is in, so the pin sinks 1.31 mA whatever the chip is doing. The user guide SLAU869E says it in the jumper table: "J10: OFF if pin initialized as output low or input with pullup or pulldown" (the same for J9 and PA0). **Tag: Our mistake.** With PA1 high the same STANDBY0 image reads 0.198 mA, which is the thermistor divider and the light-sensor circuit, not the chip. Before any power run on this board: read table 2-1 of the user guide, pull J9 and J10 or keep PA0 and PA1 high, and expect about 0.2 mA of board circuits on top of the chip. The tool's scale was never in doubt: CoreMark at 32 MHz and 4 MHz differ by 72.9 µA per MHz against the data sheet's 71, and SLEEP0 minus SHUTDOWN is 940 µA against 978. Numbers:

### Does TI's CMSIS-DSP library run on the L1306, and what fits?

Yes. The SDK's prebuilt Cortex-M0 library ran FFTs, FIR and biquad filters with the same errors as the C code on a Mac: a 256-point q15 FFT takes 2.25 ms at 32 MHz, a 512-point one 5.2 ms. **Tag: Chip limit.** The largest transforms that fit 4 kB of RAM are 512 points in q15 and 256 in q31; a 512-point q31 FFT's buffer alone is 4 kB. A 256-point FFT in 32-bit float also runs, in software because the chip has no FPU: 25.7 ms, 11 times the q15 time.

### Why does the L1306 score 0.73 DMIPS per MHz when tables often say about 1?

Those tables usually let the compiler inline across Dhrystone's procedures, which the benchmark's rules forbid; with that on, this chip reads 1.04. And at 32 MHz the flash adds a wait state, which costs Dhrystone 17% (0.88 DMIPS per MHz at 4 MHz). **Tag: Setup or handling.** The number depends on the rules and clock you pick.

### Embench's st benchmark reports FAIL. Is the chip's maths wrong?

No. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** It fails its own check at both optimization levels on this chip and on the MSPM0G3507; on the G3507 the difference was traced to one or two steps of the last bit of a double, finer than Embench's 1e-13 tolerance. Not re-traced on the L1306.

### Can I take code written for the MSPM0G3507 and run it on the L1306?

Plain C, and code that only uses DriverLib calls both chips have, moves with SysConfig changes only: CoreMark, the occupancy models and TI's temperature example all did. **Tag: Chip limit.** What does not move is anything that needs a block the L1306 lacks (math accelerator, AES, TRNG, 12-bit DAC, CAN, port B pins) or more than 4 kB of RAM. Counts for TI's own examples:

## DriverLib, TI Drivers and Zephyr

These come from building one small app (ADC reading, serial line, LED) three ways on this board and the LP-MSPM0G3507: `portability/three-ways/README.md`. MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07, TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS, Zephyr 4.4.2.

### My TI Drivers program on the L1306 sends binary at 115200 instead of text. Why?

Not found; use DriverLib or Zephyr for serial output on this chip until it is. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Our mistake).** The image runs and keeps sending: runs of zero bytes and a repeating 32-bit word 0x0000136f at 115200, and nothing readable at six other rates from 9600 to 460800 (observed, not saved). The suspect is the hand-ported configuration, since TI ships no TI Drivers example for this chip. Ruled out: 1-byte against 32-byte UART ring buffers (no change), a missing `UART_init()` (this SDK has no such function), and the clock (a 32 MHz bus clock, confirmed by the working DriverLib build).

### TI Drivers on FreeRTOS will not link on the L1306: "run placement with alignment fails for section ".bss" size 0x1458". Why?

TI's FreeRTOS settings file for this board does not fit its 4 kB of RAM. **Tag: TI example default.** The linker needs 0x1458 (5.1 kB) of `.bss` against 0x1000 (4 kB) of RAM, mostly the 3 kB heap that TI's `FreeRTOSConfig.h` for the LP-MSPM0L1306 asks for. FreeRTOS alone fits with static allocation (`freertos/README.md`); that was not run with TI Drivers.

### Does Zephyr have an ADC driver for the MSPM0?

Not in Zephyr 4.4.2: its `drivers/adc` folder has no MSPM0 file. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** Call DriverLib from your Zephyr app for the ADC and add `dl_adc12.c` and `dl_vref.c` to `CMakeLists.txt` yourself, because Zephyr's MSPM0 Kconfig only switches on the GPIO, UART, timer and CAN parts of DriverLib. That glue is the part you rewrite for another vendor's chip.

### Zephyr's DriverLib headers differ from the MSPM0 SDK's. Does that matter?

Not for this app, as far as is known. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** In Zephyr's copy of TI's DriverLib, `dl_adc12.h` and `dl_vref.h` differ from MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07 by 143 diff lines (93 and 50, counted as the lines `diff` marks on either side); the `dl_adc12.c` and `dl_vref.c` files are identical. Inference, not checked: the differences are version drift.

### Why is MSPM0 TI Drivers configuration hand-written C?

Because MSPM0 TI Drivers have no SysConfig module: write the configuration tables in C, starting from a TI example's `ti_drivers_config.c`. **Tag: Tool or docs.** No MSPM0 TI Drivers example has a `.syscfg` file; checked by listing the 40 TI Drivers example folders in SDK 2.11.00.07 (`examples/rtos/<board>/drivers/`, 10 examples on each of four LaunchPad kits). For the same small app the configuration is 136 lines of C against 35 lines of SysConfig for DriverLib on the LP-MSPM0G3507, and 130 against 34 on this board. `portability/three-ways/README.md`, problem 3.

### Is there a TI Drivers example for the LP-MSPM0L1306?

No. **Tag: Tool or docs.** SDK 2.11.00.07 ships the driver library for this chip (`drivers_mspm0l11xx_l13xx.a`), the no-RTOS driver porting layer and a FreeRTOS settings file, but no example and no board configuration that uses them. The C configuration tables were ported from TI's G3507 `adc_singlechannel` and `uart_echo` examples (130 code lines), and the startup and linker files come from the SDK's device folder.

### A TI Drivers GPIO table entry without a pin-mux index sets up PA0. Is that expected?

Give every entry its pin-mux index, or mark it `GPIO_DO_NOT_CONFIG`. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: TI example default).** Read from the source, not run: `GPIO_init` takes the pin-mux index from each entry's low byte (`pincm = pinConfig & 0xFF`), and 0 is PA0's pin control register, which drives LED1 on this board. TI's G3507 `adc_singlechannel` table has four entries without one.

### TI Drivers' ADC driver does not turn on the internal reference. Do I have to?

Yes, as far as the source shows: turn the reference on with DriverLib in your configuration. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs).** `ADCMSPM0.c` sets the reference choice in the ADC but never touches the VREF block. Not checked on a board, because no TI Drivers image here has printed a reading.

### The CC1407P host build prints its banner and the first SPI frame on the LP-MSPM0L1306, then nothing. Is the board hung?

With no radio on SPI0 (PA6, PA5, PA4, PA3, PA7, PA2) that is the expected stop: the driver waits for the radio in the SPI-complete handler (halted in `hb_delay_us`, 3 s after reset). **Tag: Setup or handling.** Wire the BP-CC1407P-9-FE as in `mspm0l1306/radio-host/README.md`; the first frame `00 04 11 00 02 32 00 00 e9 71` is the same ten bytes the LP-MSPM0G5187 sent in its recorded link. Build with the pool cut to 4 buffers (`NBUF=4`, the default there): TI's 24 need 5,244 B of the chip's 4,096 B. Run 2026-10-24, no radio attached, so the link itself is untested here.

## Setting up CCStudio and the AI on a Mac

These come from setting up CCStudio 21.0.1, the MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07 and Claude Code inside CCStudio on the same Intel Mac (macOS 15.7.9) on 2026-10-04, before the board was plugged in. They are the setup steps of the [Blink project's Start here box](../site/project-blink.html#start).

### How much free disk do I need for CCStudio and the MSPM0 SDK?

Have 12 GB free before you start, and delete each installer file once it has finished. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The full CCStudio install with every chip family is 8.1 GB, more than the 6.0 GB TI's page recommends, and the SDK adds 2.2 GB; together 10.3 GB once installed, more while an installer file sits beside its install. A Mac that started with 13 GB free dropped to 2.5 GB after CCStudio with its installer still on disk. Measured sizes: `mac-setup/README.md`, "Disk space you need".

### I clicked the MSPM0 SDK download and nothing happened in CCStudio. Where is it?

Look in your browser's downloads folder. The SDK file (`mspm0_sdk_2_11_00_07.app.zip`, 0.4 GB) downloads in the browser from ti.com/tool/MSPM0-SDK, not inside CCStudio; unzip it and run the installer. **Tag: Tool or docs.** CCStudio's first screen gives no hint that an SDK is needed, so it is easy to look for the download inside CCStudio. The padlock beside each file on TI's page marks a short export approval form, about a minute.

### CCStudio lists no SDK after I installed the MSPM0 SDK and turned on the AI. What do I do?

Quit CCStudio and open it again. **Tag: Tool or docs.** On CCStudio 21.0.1 it listed no SDK until it was restarted; after the restart it listed all six installed SDKs, the MSPM0 SDK among them. Observed 2026-10-04.

### Should I pick Global or Workspace for Scope in CCStudio's AI panel?

Pick Workspace. **Tag: Tool or docs.** CCStudio's AI panel opens on Global, and the panel itself does not say which file each choice changes. Global writes into `~/.claude/settings.json`, the settings file every other Claude Code run on the Mac uses; Workspace keeps the change inside the CCStudio workspace folder.

### Several Claude Code chat panels opened in CCStudio. Is something wrong?

No. Close the extras; one chat is enough. **Tag: Unknown.** Extra panels can open during setup; the cause was not found. The chat answered, and CCStudio's four tool servers for the AI (project, debug, SysConfig, serial) all responded afterwards.

### Does the LP-MSPM0L1306 come with a USB cable, and will it fit my Mac?

TI's user guide lists one micro-USB cable in the box (SLAU869E, section 1.3.1); the plug type on the computer end is not stated. **Tag: Setup or handling.** If it does not fit a USB-C-only Mac, use a USB-C to micro-B cable or an adapter. An LP-MSPM0G3507 came with a cable that had a USB-A plug on the computer end.

### Does this work on an Apple Silicon Mac?

Not tested. **Tag: Unknown.** Every time and size on this page and in the Blink Start here box comes from one Intel MacBook (Core i7-8750H) on macOS 15.7.9. TI's download page offers CCStudio and the MSPM0 SDK for macOS; neither was run on an Apple Silicon Mac.

## Benchmark programs

### Why does the PID power loop on the LP-MSPM0L1306 miss periods at 100 kHz in Q15 when it is clean at 10 kHz?

Run the Q15 loop at 92 kHz or below: a rate sweep on the board found 92.75 kHz the highest rate with no missed period in 1,000, and at 50 kHz about 57 percent of the CPU is left for other work. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** Only code in flash at -O2 was tried. The lead: each interrupt takes 273.5 cycles of CPU with entry and return, and the ADC takes about 65 cycles from trigger to interrupt, about 338 together, close to the 345-count period the sweep found. At 32 MHz, the chip's top clock, a 100 kHz period is 320 cycles, and the loop's worst time from trigger to the end of the interrupt was 313. In the 100 kHz pass 6 of 1,000 interrupts ran past the end of their period, and one ADC result was overwritten before it was read. Interrupt entry took up to 152 cycles in that pass against at most 59 in the 10 kHz pass, which suggests some interrupts started late; why was not found. The 10 kHz pass had no such period and the same 228-cycle mean. MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07, TI Arm Clang 5.1.1 -O2, code in flash; rows in `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`.

### How fast can the LP-MSPM0L1306 run the C2000's FOC motor-control loop?

1.83 kHz in software float and 16.94 kHz with TI's IQmath fixed-point library, each the highest rate with no missed period in 1,000, found by a rate sweep on the board. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** The Cortex-M0+ has no floating-point unit and this chip has no math accelerator, so every sine and cosine is software; a sine lookup table was not run. The float run at a 50 kHz trigger stopped at the program's time limit after 80 of 1,000 interrupts, so its worst case, 13k cycles from trigger to PWM value (4,131.2 percent of a 100 kHz period), rests on those 80, where the angle stayed under 0.8 radians. The older 1,000-interrupt run at 1 kHz, same `foc.c`, reached 17k cycles (5,399.7 percent). For scale, the LAUNCHXL-F2800137 holds the same loop at 301.5 kHz from flash. TI Arm Clang 5.1.1 -O2, 32 MHz, code in flash; rows in `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`.

### Should I run my control loop from RAM on the LP-MSPM0L1306 to skip the flash wait state?

Only if every routine the loop calls fits in RAM with it. The FOC step in TI's IQmath ran 2.6% faster from RAM (1,744.9 cycles against 1,700.2), but the float step ran 6.3% slower (12,701.1 against 13,497.3), because its library routines do not all fit the 4 kB SRAM (the map shows it 3.9 kB full, with the double-precision helpers left in flash) and each call between SRAM and flash goes through a trampoline of about 12 cycles. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** Only one stack size was built; a smaller stack might fit the helpers too. With the flash prefetch and cache on (the reset setting), code in flash costs only about 3% here. TI Arm Clang 5.1.1 -O2, 32 MHz, measured 2026-10-08.

### SYSCTL MCLKCFG on the LP-MSPM0L1306 reads FLASHWAIT 2 at 32 MHz. Does it run with two flash wait states?

No, it runs with one: ignore the `FLASHWAIT` field on this chip. **Tag: Tool or docs.** The field only applies when the main clock comes from HSCLK, which the MSPM0L130x does not have; with the clock from SYSOSC the hardware picks the wait state itself, and the data sheet gives 0 up to 24 MHz and 1 up to 32 MHz. The register reads 0x00000200 after TI's SysConfig clock code; driverlib's `dl_sysctl_mspm0l11xx_l13xx.h` says "Flash wait states are managed automatically by SYSCTL when MCLK is running from SYSOSC or LFCLK". MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07.

### Is GCC as fast as TI Arm Clang on the LP-MSPM0L1306?

No: CoreMark at -O3 and 32 MHz scores 78.27 with TI Arm Clang 5.1.1 and 54.62 with GCC 12.2.0 (the Zephyr SDK's), bare metal, the same source files, both validated. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The compiler and C library you pick move this score by 43% (TI Arm Clang with its own library against GCC with newlib-nano; the compiler alone was not separated); with `-funroll-loops` GCC reaches 58.65. The SDK's GCC startup file and linker script build it with no changes. Measured 2026-10-08; rows in `data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`.

### I read my benchmark's results from the LP-MSPM0L1306 with a second OpenOCD call after the run, and got all zeros. Did the run fail?

Probably not: read the results from the SRAM dump taken in the same OpenOCD connection as the run, not with a new connection. **Tag: Setup or handling.** A second OpenOCD call restarts the chip as it connects, and the start-up code zeroes the results array (`fom`, at 0x20000800), so the read gives zeros. The same connection's dump (`sram.bin`) holds the finished array; read results from the dump. xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0+dev.

### The SPI speed test on the LP-MSPM0L1306 stops after its first two passes and never sets its done marker. Is the SPI broken?

No: the two CPU-fed passes at 16 MHz, the chip's maximum, completed and give 1,644 kB/s with 8-bit frames and 1,785 kB/s with 16-bit frames. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: the DMA setup for this chip's SPI0).** The next pass is the first DMA-fed one; it and every later pass (the 8 MHz passes and the loopback check) read zero, and the done marker stayed 0 (`spi: magic 0x0 (NOT DONE)`). The same code runs to the end on the MSPM0G3507.

<!-- recovery:start -->
## When the board stops answering

Checked 2026-11-08. Before flashing a risky image, run `python3 tools/preflight_image.py <board id> <image.out>`. Narrative and commands: `docs/remote-board-recovery.md`.

How it locks up:

- An image enters SHUTDOWN right after boot: DAP Connection Error, low power mode (`mspm0l1306/FAQ.md`)
- A window-watchdog example resets the chip every few milliseconds: Could not find MEM-AP (`mspm0l1306/FAQ.md`, `ports/cms32/README.md`)
- A deep-sleep port with only the watchdog timer as wake source (ran, woke every 0.997 s) (`ports/msp430-to-mspm0/lpm3-wake/PORT.md`, 2026-10-21)
- TI timx_timer_mode_periodic_standby enters STANDBY: every debugger read answers ack 4, and a reset pulse with a halt does not catch it (`docs/experiments/2026-11-06-mspm0l1306-live-chip-view.md`, 2026-11-06)
- Found silent: OpenOCD could not attach (FRL-E006), frl identify saw no answer on SWD or JTAG (FRL-E010), an OpenOCD reset halt returned nothing; the same signature as the STANDBY lockup. Which image was on the board is not known (the last recorded run was the 2026-11-06 live chip view). Recovered the same day with the DSLite method below: the chip answered after the write; DSLite's own verify step fails with 'Memory map prevented reading 0x0000FFF8', so the proof is an OpenOCD read-back (backup.py save), which matched the written image (`mspm0l1306/FAQ.md`, 2026-11-08)

Try in this order. Remote means the Mac does it with the board in place; hands means a person unplugs, presses or moves something.

| Method | Remote or hands | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hold S1 (PA18), press and release S3 (reset), keep S1 held 2 s, then flash a non-sleeping image at once; replug USB afterwards (for the SHUTDOWN lockup; the chip then starts in the ROM bootloader until a plain power cycle) | hands | proven | `mspm0l1306/FAQ.md`, `mspm0l1306/AGENTS.md`, date not recorded |
| OpenOCD mailbox mass erase (mspm0_mass_erase) (for the watchdog reset loop) | remote | proven | `mspm0l1306/FAQ.md`, date not recorded |
| OpenOCD mailbox mass erase (for the SHUTDOWN lockup: OpenOCD exits when the debug port fails to answer) | remote | failed | `mspm0l1306/FAQ.md`, date not recorded |
| uhubctl power-off of the probe port (the tick counter restarted; the hub location is not recorded) | remote | proven | 2026-10-21 |
| DSLite flash from UniFlash 9.6.0 with a non-sleeping image and the board ccxml (for the STANDBY lockup; the first try worked, no hands; second success 2026-11-08 (the 2026-11-02 backup image written back; expect DSLite's verify to fail at 0xFFF8 and check with backup.py instead; the image path must contain no space)) | remote | proven | `docs/experiments/2026-11-06-mspm0l1306-live-chip-view.md`, 2026-11-08 |

USB hub ports recorded for this board:

- The probe's hub port does not cut power, 2026-10-27. SRAM marker test: a word written at 0x20000FF0 through the DAP (no CPU connect, no reset) survived a 15 s `uhubctl -a off`; the chip and the XDS110 kept power. The port does drop the data link: the probe leaves USB within 1 s and is back 1.0 s after `on` on every port of this hub (nine ports tried), and the first debugger connect after a cut answers Error -261, the second works.

<!-- recovery:end -->

## Watching the chip run (live chip view)

### Which browsers and boards does the chip view work on?

Chrome or Edge on a Mac, Windows or Linux computer, with an LP-MSPM0L1306, LP-MSPM0G3507, LP-MSPM0G3519 or LP-MSPM0G5187 plugged in over USB. **Tag: Chip limit.** The page reaches the board's XDS110 probe through WebHID, which Safari and Firefox do not have. Close CCStudio, UniFlash and OpenOCD first, because only one program can hold the probe. The view has been read live on the L1306, G3519 and G5187, with CPU load checked against a known load only on the L1306 ([E317](docs/experiments/2026-11-06-mspm0l1306-live-chip-view.md)).

### Does the chip view halt or slow my program? Does it change a power measurement?

It does not halt, reset or write to the chip, and it costs the program no instructions, but do not measure power while it is attached. **Tag: Chip limit.** The reads go through the debug port beside the CPU. The debug connection can keep the chip out of its deepest sleep, so the current you measure is not the current of the program alone. A program that enters STANDBY drops the debug link; the page then says "Not answering". If every read answers "ack 4", flash a program that does not sleep with TI's DSLite from UniFlash 9.6 and the board's ccxml. [E317](docs/experiments/2026-11-06-mspm0l1306-live-chip-view.md)

### The view shows addresses like 0x00000234 instead of function names. Where do I get the names?

Choose the program's .out file in the page. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The chip does not store function names, only code, so the page can show the address the CPU is on. The .out is the build output that CCStudio or `make` writes in the project's Debug folder. The page reads it in the browser to turn addresses into names.

### The page says "This page has no map for this chip yet". Which chips are covered?

Four: the MSPM0L1306, MSPM0G3507, MSPM0G3519 and MSPM0G5187. **Tag: Chip limit.** A map is a file of the chip's blocks, pins and interrupts, made from the SDK headers. The page matches the chip's DEVICEID against the maps, and a chip without one is refused. Other MSPM0 chips need a new map file.

### Why does a PWM pin show no rate, or show "fast"?

A pin driven by a timer does not change its output register, so there is no rate to count; the page shows the timer's period instead. **Tag: Chip limit.** A pin that the program switches in software shows "fast" when it changes more than about 100 times a second, because the page reads the port about 500 times a second and cannot count more than that. TI's PWM example read a 16.0 ms period from its timer registers (load 1999, prescale 256, 32 MHz).

### Does the chip view work with my own program?

Yes, with no change to it, as long as the program does not put the chip into a sleep deep enough to drop the debug link. **Tag: Setup or handling.** Load, powered blocks, pin setup, slow pin changes and the running code were read from TI's own examples, a CoreMark build and a test program; none needed a change. A program that enters STANDBY or SHUTDOWN needs the recovery above.

==============================================================================
FILE: mspm0l1306/AGENTS.md | AI assistant notes for the TI LP-MSPM0L1306 LaunchPad development kit
==============================================================================

# AI assistant notes for the TI LP-MSPM0L1306 LaunchPad development kit

The 4 kB of RAM runs out long before anything else, and that a few silent traps (stack size, Zephyr's heap, missing interrupt lines, one ignored SysConfig line) cost hours if nobody warns it. This file is the short list, each item comes from runs on one board unless it says otherwise.

Terms: [docs/vocab.md](../docs/vocab.md) and the [LP-MSPM0L1306 FAQ](FAQ.md) in the Fox Red Labs repo. In short: **SysConfig** is TI's tool that writes a chip's pin and clock setup code; **DriverLib** is TI's C library for the chip's parts; **NONMAIN** is the flash area that holds the chip's boot settings; **CoreMark** is a standard CPU speed test; **MessagePack** is a compact binary format for structured data; **MEM-AP** is the debug port the debugger uses to reach the CPU; **static allocation** means RAM is reserved when the program is built, not requested while it runs. 1 kB = 1,024 bytes. Checked 2026-10-06 on an Intel Mac, macOS 15.7.9, with MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07, TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS, SysConfig 1.26.3, xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0+dev and Zephyr 4.4.2, on one LP-MSPM0L1306.

**How to use it.** Copy this file into the top folder of your own project as `AGENTS.md`. Most coding assistants read that name; for one that reads `CLAUDE.md`, copy it under that name or add the line `@AGENTS.md` to your `CLAUDE.md`. Paths below in backticks starting `mspm0l1306/` or `data/` are in the Fox Red Labs repo; they are not in your copy, and links in this file only work inside that repo.

## The board

| Part | Fact |
|---|---|
| Chip | MSPM0L1306: Arm Cortex-M0+, 32 MHz from the internal oscillator, one flash wait state above 24 MHz (`mspm0l1306/README.md`) |
| Memory | 64 kB flash, 4 kB RAM. Flash was never the limit; RAM always was (`mspm0l1306/README.md`) |
| Not on the chip | No FPU, no divide instruction, no math accelerator, no AES, no random-number generator, no radio, no general-purpose DAC (only the comparator's 8-bit reference DAC). Hardware CRC is there (`data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`) |
| Interrupt lines | Only 0, 1, 2, 4, 9, 13, 15, 16, 18, 20, 24, 25 and 31 exist (`mspm0l1306/FAQ.md`) |
| LEDs | LED1 red on PA0 (on when the pin is low); LED2 color on PA26 red, PA13 green, PA27 blue (`mspm0l1306/zephyr/README.md`) |
| Buttons | S1 on PA18 (held at reset, starts TI's serial bootloader), S2 on PA14, S3 reset (`mspm0l1306/FAQ.md`) |
| Sensors | Light sensor (photodiode into op-amp 0, PA22, PA24, PA25); thermistor on PA15 (`data/results/mspm0l1306.csv`) |
| Serial | UART0 on PA8 (TX) and PA9 (RX). Jumpers J16 and J17 on XDS (right, as shipped) send it to the USB serial port; on BP (left) to the header pins (`mspm0l1306/FAQ.md`) |
| Debugger | XDS110 on the board, USB, two serial ports, no driver needed on a Mac (`mspm0l1306/README.md`) |

A labeled picture of every part: `mspm0l1306/img/board-tour.png`.

## Start here

| Step | This board |
|---|---|
| Whole route | `./start.sh mspm0l1306 blink --probe <serial>` does the rows below in order with no assistant (`docs/frl.md`); stops with FRL-E002 if several probes are plugged in and none is named |
| Tools | MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07, TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS (from CCStudio 21.0.1), SysConfig 1.26.3, xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7 (the first with `ti_mspm0.cfg`; `tools/frl` runs later versions only when named, as unvalidated), UniFlash 9.6.0 (`mspm0l1306/README.md`) |
| Probe serial | `python3 tools/frl/frl.py detect`, or `xdsdfu -e` from CCStudio's `ccs_base/common/uscif/xds110/` folder |
| Back up | `python3 tools/benchmark/backup.py save mspm0l1306 --probe <serial>` (tested recipe: main flash and NONMAIN read twice and compared; NONMAIN is never written back) |
| Build TI's blink | `cp -R <SDK>/examples/nortos/LP_MSPM0L1306/driverlib/gpio_toggle_output .` then `make -C gpio_toggle_output/ticlang MSPM0_SDK_INSTALL_DIR=<SDK> SYSCONFIG_TOOL=/Applications/ti/sysconfig_1.26.3/sysconfig_cli.sh TICLANG_ARMCOMPILER=/Applications/ti/ccs2101/ccs/tools/compiler/ti-cgt-armllvm_5.1.1.LTS GCC_ARMCOMPILER=` (3.3 s) |
| Flash | `openocd -f interface/xds110.cfg -c "adapter serial <serial>" -c "adapter speed 2500" -f target/ti_mspm0.cfg -c init -c "reset halt" -c "program gpio_toggle_output/ticlang/gpio_toggle_output.out verify" -c "reset run" -c shutdown` (0.6 s) |
| Check | `python3 tools/check/blink.py --board mspm0l1306 --probe <serial>` |
